results.title: Emirates to resume Bahrain flights but Kuwait services remain suspended | The National
results.body:
Etihad cited safety as its foremost concern, saying: "The safety and comfort of our guests and crew is our number one priority."

Emirates is set to resume flights between Dubai and Bahrain from Saturday, August 15, after weeks of cancellations owing to regional tensions.

The airline currently lists one service, EK839, departing Dubai International Airport at 4pm and arriving in Bahrain at 4.20pm local time. The return marks a limited resumption of a route on which Emirates previously operated three daily services. Its other two scheduled Bahrain flights, EK835 and EK837, remain cancelled for now.

Emirates services between Dubai and Kuwait remain suspended, however, with no flights currently listed on the airline's website. The airline had previously suspended all three of its daily Bahrain services, as well as four daily Kuwait flights - EK853, EK855, EK857 and EK859 - amid regional tensions and disruption in the Gulf.

A disclaimer on the airline's website states: "Please be aware that we can only show the services offered on Emirates-operated flights. For any connecting flights operated by codeshare airlines, please refer to their website."

Etihad Airways, which previously operated multiple daily services between Abu Dhabi and Bahrain, is currently operating a reduced schedule on the route.

Flights EY643 and EY644 between Zayed International Airport and Bahrain International Airport will continue to operate as scheduled. However, three other return services - EY641-EY642, EY645-EY646 and EY647-EY648 - have been cancelled until August 21.

The airline said affected passengers would be assisted with alternative travel arrangements, including rebooking on other services.

Etihad is also operating one daily flight to Kuwait, with EY653 scheduled to depart Abu Dhabi at 8.25am.

Fellow UAE carriers flydubai and Air Arabia also operate services to Bahrain and Kuwait, although some flights are subject to cancellation.

Meanwhile, Qatar Airways has also resumed daily services to Bahrain, Kuwait and Erbil. The airline has continued to operate flights between Doha and the UAE throughout the latest disruption, serving Dubai, Abu Dhabi and Sharjah.

From Kuwait, Kuwait Airways and Jazeera Airways continue to operate multiple daily services to Dubai and Abu Dhabi, while Bahrain's Gulf Air maintains flights to both UAE cities.

The disruption is not limited to UAE airlines. While hopes of de-escalation have grown, the US and Iran continue to exchange threats after months of attacks. International carriers have had to adjust schedules because of airspace restrictions and operational uncertainty across the region.

Air Canada has extended the suspension of its flights to Tel Aviv and Dubai until mid-January 2027. KLM has suspended services to Dubai, Riyadh and Dammam until September 6 as it continues to avoid flying through the airspace of Iran, Iraq, Israel and parts of the Arabian Gulf. Lufthansa Group airlines, including Lufthansa and Swiss, have also adjusted schedules to several Middle East destinations in recent weeks, while Air France has temporarily suspended flights to Saudi Arabia.

Airlines have referred to security concerns, airspace restrictions and operational uncertainty as they continue to review their schedules.

results.title: A nation between adversaries
results.body:
PAKISTAN is currently in the global spotlight for mediating between the United States and Iran. Islamabad's rigorous mediation efforts helped bring about a much-needed ceasefire between the US and Iran in April, which culminated in the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding in June 2026. Analysts see the current mediatory position as a new shift in Pakistan's foreign policy priorities, with Islamabad attempting to assert itself as a middle power and a relevant strategic player in Middle Eastern geopolitics. However, a comprehensive historical analysis reveals that mediation has remained one of Pakistan's most essential foreign policy imperatives.

Pakistan has long adopted an active strategy of mediation to prevent, manage, and settle disputes in the Middle East and within its immediate western neighbourhood. Far from being a passive regional actor, Islamabad has often positioned itself as a mediator in conflicts ranging from great-power rivalries to intra-Muslim problems. This approach is based on a deliberate foreign policy calculus determined by geography, strategic alliances, and the need to protect national interests while expanding diplomatic influence beyond South Asia.

The logic behind Pakistan's mediating role

The primary strategic motive behind Pakistan's mediation diplomacy is the need to keep regional disputes from spilling over onto its own borders. Unlike great powers, which may approach mediation largely for geopolitical or ideological reasons, Pakistan's security is immediately influenced by conflicts in its near neighbourhood. Regional conflicts have historically been accompanied by refugee flows, cross-border terrorism, interruption of trade routes, arms trafficking, narcotics smuggling, and humanitarian crises, all of which have imposed significant economic and security costs on Pakistan. For Islamabad, mediation, therefore, constitutes a preventive tactic meant to contain problems before they evolve into greater challenges to Pakistan itself.

Afghanistan is a glaring example of this security rationale. For over four decades, Afghanistan's instability has had far-reaching implications for Pakistan, including inflow of millions of refugees, increased terrorism and border insecurity, and enhanced economic burden. As a result, Pakistan expended enormous diplomatic capital in promoting the intra-Afghan peace process, as well as talks between the Taliban and the US. Islamabad's coordination and facilitation resulted in the 2020 Doha Agreement. These efforts were primarily motivated by Islamabad's desire to construct a relatively stable Afghanistan capable of denying space to transnational terrorist organisations and minimising fears of long-term instability along the Pakistan-Afghan border. Thus, mediation is a strategic investment in Pakistan's domestic security.

A comprehensive historical analysis reveals that mediation has remained one of Pakistan's most essential foreign policy imperatives.

A similar rationale supports Pakistan's efforts to defuse tensions in the Middle East, particularly efforts to reduce tensions between Iran and Saudi Arabia. Pakistan shares a lengthy border with Iran while also maintaining strong strategic ties with Saudi Arabia and the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) states. The signing of the Strategic Mutual Defence Agreement in 2025 has further increased Pakistan's geopolitical stakes in the Middle Eastern security environment, as has the recent mutual defence pact with Turkiye and Saudi Arabia. Any escalation between Tehran and Riyadh could place Pakistan in a perilous strategic position. These confrontations have often exposed Islamabad to opposing geopolitical realities, as well as exacerbating local sectarian tensions. The 1990s era of sectarian violence has had a significant impact on Pakistan's strategic thinking. Islamabad doesn't want to allow space for another wave of sectarian violence influenced by the Middle Eastern security environment.

This is why Pakistan has continuously pursued a policy of passive or active mediation between Saudi Arabia and Iran. For instance in 2016, when tensions between Saudi Arabia and Iran escalated due to the execution of a famous Saudi Shia cleric, Sheikh Nimr al-Nimr, Pakistan hurried to utilise shuttle diplomacy to defuse tensions. Pakistan's then-prime minister Nawaz Sharif and chief of army staff Raheel Sharif advocated holding direct discussions between Saudi Arabia and Iran in Islamabad and recommended that both countries establish focal persons to keep communication lines open for dialogue. These activities were widely considered as an effective tool for reducing tensions between Saudi Arabia and Iran.

Similarly, in June 2017, a Saudi-led quartet (also including the United Arab Emirates, Bahrain, and Egypt) broke diplomatic relations and implemented a rigorous land, air, and sea blockade against Qatar. Saudi Arabia put enormous pressure on Pakistan to take Riyadh's side. Rather than supporting the blockade, Pakistan maintained its neutral posture and initiated a joint diplomatic push with Kuwait and Turkiye to ease tensions between Qatar and the Saudi-led quad. Although the attempts did not yield significant results, they did reduce pressure on Pakistan's foreign policy.

Similarly, following strikes on Saudi oil sites in 2019, the then-prime minister Imran Khan conducted shuttle diplomacy between Tehran and Riyadh in an effort to ease tensions and foster dialogue. Although Pakistan was not the primary architect of the ultimate Saudi-Iranian rapprochement, its diplomatic efforts highlighted Islamabad's preference for regional de-escalation over bloc politics. More recently, Pakistan's co-mediation with Qatar in supporting US-Iran negotiations under the Islamabad MoU demonstrated its broader goal of preventing another potentially destabilising conflict in its western neighbourhood.

Secondly, Pakistan's mediation diplomacy strengthens its strategic relevance within an increasingly competitive international system. As global politics grows more polarised, middle powers seek influence through diplomatic rather than coercive means. Pakistan positions itself as a responsible regional partner or net security stabiliser, capable of maintaining communication lines in situations where direct dialogue has become politically challenging. Islamabad believes that successful mediation in regional conflicts can boost Pakistan's diplomatic profile by presenting it as a proactive rather than reactive actor in regional disputes. This is especially relevant in the context of global preferences to look at Pakistan through the security and counterterrorism lenses. Mediation allows Islamabad to change global perceptions by demonstrating diplomatic ability and a commitment to peaceful conflict settlement.

Pakistan also wants to demonstrate it strategic value to major powers through mediation. High-profile facilitation operations, such as organising Henry Kissinger's secret 1971 visit to Beijing, highlighted Pakistan's ability to bridge the gap between Washington and Beijing. As of today, Beijing recognises Pakistan's facilitation efforts, which have improved its status in Washington and Beijing.

Islamabad has been consistently seeking strategic goodwill in the international community. States that successfully facilitate negotiations frequently collect diplomatic capital, which can later be used to gain political support, strengthen bilateral relations, or increase influence within multilateral institutions. Pakistan's active participation in facilitating dialogue in Afghanistan, and encouraging regional de-escalation in the Middle East, allows it to strengthen ties with a wide range of international actors, including the US, China, Gulf states, Central Asian republics, and Muslim-majority countries. The diplomatic goodwill broadens Pakistan's foreign policy options while reducing the likelihood of strategic isolation.

Islamabad believes that an active mediatory role in regional conflicts can protect and further secure Pakistan's long-term economic interests. Regional instability discourages foreign direct investment, interrupts trade corridors, increases international trade insurance costs, and causes large infrastructure projects to be delayed. As Pakistan strives to transform itself into a regional connectivity hub through projects like the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC), peace in neighbouring regions has become an economic necessity rather than a diplomatic aspiration. Stability in Afghanistan is critical for developing overland trade with Central Asia, while lower tensions between the Gulf states and Iran can improve the security of Pakistan's energy imports, and enhance the utility of Gwadar port. As a result, mediation indirectly helps to create an external environment that promotes economic growth and regional integration for Islamabad. Furthermore, effective diplomatic engagement can boost investors' confidence by portraying Pakistan as a stabilising rather than destabilising regional actor. International investors often prefer regions with political certainty and amicable interstate relations.

Finally, Pakistan's mediation efforts are motivated by its overall diplomatic identity. Since independence, succeeding governments have continuously prioritised peaceful conflict resolution, negotiation, and negotiated agreements in their official foreign policy rhetoric. Individual mediation initiatives are definitely shaped by geopolitical goals, but Pakistan has often depicted itself as a country eager to provide good offices whenever conflicts endanger regional peace and international security. Whether facilitating dialogue in Afghanistan, encouraging Saudi-Iran engagement, or launching a diplomatic initiative to defuse tensions between the US and Iran, Islamabad has sought to position itself as a bridge between competing actors rather than a participant in regional rivalries.

The historical record

Pakistan's diplomatic role as a successful mediator or back-channel facilitator started in late 1969 when Islamabad facilitated the US-China rapprochement. Pakistan facilitated a secret historic visit of Henry Kissinger to Beijing. The visit paved the way for US-China diplomatic and economic engagement, which dramatically reshaped Cold War geopolitics. This episode remains a typical successful example of Pakistan using its contacts to achieve a significant diplomatic outcome.

In Afghanistan's context, Pakistan was a key player in the 1988 Geneva Accords, alongside Afghanistan, the Soviet Union, and the United States. The accords ultimately resulted in the evacuation of Soviet forces from Afghanistan's territory. This outcome is widely recognised as Pakistan's most significant multilateral diplomatic achievement. More recent initiatives have produced mixed outcomes. Pakistan facilitated the 2015 Murree peace talks, which were the first publicly acknowledged direct engagement between the Afghan government and the Afghan Taliban. However the process eventually halted. Throughout the protracted Afghan peace process (2009-2020), Pakistan continuously promoted negotiations and backed the Doha Agreement. Islamabad's initial coordination and efforts to bring the Afghan Taliban and the US to the negotiation table eventually resulted in a US-Taliban pact. However, Pakistan's efforts did not result in a comprehensive intra-Afghan settlement.

Limits of Pakistan's mediation

Despite Pakistan's long history of promoting dialogue and providing good offices in regional and international conflicts, its overall success rate remains low. According to a qualitative assessment of Pakistan's mediation record, only about one-third of its initiatives have resulted in concrete diplomatic outcomes, with the majority focusing on confidence-building, maintaining communication channels, or preventing further deterioration of warring parties' relationships rather than achieving comprehensive conflict resolution. This lower success rate does not reflect lack of diplomatic expertise, but rather the institutional and structural limits Pakistan faces.

One of the main issues is that Pakistan frequently mediates highly complex disputes. Conflicts such as the intra-Afghan conflict, external invasions in Afghanistan, Saudi-Iran tensions, Middle Eastern conflicts, and US-Iran tensions involve various stakeholders with competing strategic goals that cannot be resolved only by external mediation. Mediators can facilitate discourse, but they cannot compel opposing parties to compromise when the political costs of concessions are excessively high. As a result, Pakistan's participation has frequently been restricted to facilitating negotiations, with ultimate decisions determined primarily by warring parties on their own political and strategic calculations.

Another important restraint is Pakistan's low diplomatic leverage in comparison to other regional and extra-regional countries. Successful mediation frequently necessitates the capacity to offer economic incentives, security guarantees, reconstruction assistance, or political assurances that motivate opposing parties to reach difficult concessions. Countries with significantly more financial resources, political power, and diplomatic networks to sustain long-term peace initiatives include the US, China, Norway, Qatar, the UAE, and Saudi Arabia. In contrast, Pakistan typically focuses on persuasion, trusted relationships, and geographical familiarity rather than economic incentives. While these assets are valuable, they are largely insufficient to resolve longstanding disputes.

Pakistan's internal security environment further complicates mediation efforts. Persistent tensions with India, ongoing instability along the Pak-Afghan border, menace of terrorism, and periodic economic crises all divert diplomatic focus and reduce the resources available for long-term international mediation. Effective mediation is a long-term process that requires consistent diplomatic engagement, technical expertise, and institutional capacity. Pakistan's diplomatic machinery usually operates with competing internal and regional environments. This makes it difficult to maintain long-term involvement in various peace processes.

Perceptions of neutrality also challenge Pakistan's mediatory efforts in Middle Eastern conflicts. Theoretically, for mediation efforts to be successful, all parties must believe that the mediator is impartial and trustworthy. However, Pakistan's deep strategic ties with Saudi Arabia and other Arab Gulf states often cause concern among opposing parties. For example, Pakistan's longstanding defence and security partnership with Saudi Arabia has historically hampered its ability to be perceived as completely neutral by Iran, despite Islamabad's consistent efforts to maintain cordial relations with both nations. Similarly, Pakistan's extensive engagement with the Afghan Taliban has occasionally prompted segments of the former Afghan political elite and some Western policymakers to question Islamabad's neutrality, even though Pakistan actively encouraged negotiations and political settlements in Afghanistan prior to the fall of Kabul in 2021. These perceptions, whether accurate or not, frequently undermine the warring parties' willingness to fully embrace Pakistani mediation.

The geopolitical climate further limits Pakistan's effectiveness as a mediator. Many recent conflicts are increasingly impacted by great power competition, and leave little diplomatic space for middle powers to independently secure comprehensive settlements. The Afghan peace process, for example, brought together the strategic interests of the US, China, Russia, Iran, India, Qatar, and numerous other Gulf states. Similarly, the ongoing conflict between Iran and the US is driven by larger issues such as nuclear proliferation, sanctions, Israel's security, insecurity of GCC states and regional proxy conflict. In such cases, Pakistan can encourage dialogue and propose confidence-building measures, but it lacks the ability to address the underlying strategic calculations that drive the conflict.

Another rationale for Pakistan's relatively low success rate is the nature of the mediation role Islamabad normally adopts. Unlike well-established and well-known mediators such as Qatar, the UAE, and Norway, who aim to reach binding agreements, Pakistan has frequently served as a facilitator, host, bridge-builder, or provider of good offices. These roles are less apparent yet nevertheless diplomatically significant. Facilitators generate opportunities for dialogue, provide conducive environment for dialogue, establish communication channels and decrease misperceptions. Although these measures may not result in landmark peace treaties, they frequently keep preventing crises from escalating into broader armed conflict. Hence, measuring Pakistan's mediation record exclusively based on the number of signed agreements understates its overall contribution to regional stability.

Finally, Pakistan's mediation activities have occasionally suffered from a lack of follow-up by the opposing parties themselves. Several times negotiations brokered by Pakistan began with hope but later disintegrated due to one or more sides withdrawing due to their domestic political factors or altered external or regional developments. Pakistan's mediatory experience in intra-Afghan dialogue exemplifies this challenge. Although Pakistan played a crucial role in supporting the Doha talks, the subsequent political trajectory in Afghanistan, combined with deteriorating Pakistan-Afghanistan relations after 2021, proved that successful mediation does not guarantee long-term peace. Similarly, Pakistan's efforts to de-escalate tensions between Saudi Arabia and Iran in 2016 and 2019 were overshadowed by broader regional forces before China helped broker the 2023 diplomatic reconciliation.

Nevertheless, Pakistan's moderate success rate as a mediator should not be regarded as diplomatic failure. International mediation is inherently risky, and even the most experienced mediators have struggled to reach long-term settlements in prolonged conflicts. Pakistan's comparative advantage is less in imposing solutions than preserving dialogue when contact between adversaries has broken down. Despite Islamabad's structural limitations, its geographic proximity, long-standing regional relationships, understanding of local political dynamics of Iran and Afghanistan, and ability to maintain engagement with mutually hostile actors such as Saudi Arabia and Iran are valuable diplomatic assets. As regional crises become more frequent, Pakistan's role as a facilitator and confidence-builder is likely to remain a significant component of Islamabad's foreign policy strategy.

The writer is a strategic analyst of international security. The views expressed are his own.

results.title: Festa do Monte
results.body:
A tradição volta a cumprir-se esta noite, 14 de Agosto, no Monte, onde locais, turistas e emigrantes fazem a festa em honra da padroeira da Madeira.

A festa de Nossa Senhora do Monte data dos primórdios da colonização da ilha e é considerada o maior e mais concorrido arraial cristão da Madeira, sendo que a devoção dos madeirenses está ligada a um momento trágico na história da ilha, quando uma aluvião registada em 1803 provocou a morte de aproximadamente mil pessoas. Para ajudar a enfrentar esta calamidade, a diocese do Funchal considerou, no ano seguinte, a Senhora do Monte como a padroeira da Madeira.

A Festa de Nossa Senhora do Monte tem como um dos momentos centrais as celebrações religiosas do dia 15, incluindo a Missa Solene e a Procissão de Nossa Senhora do Monte.

Mas outros eventos estão marcados para hoje e que pode marcar na sua agenda:

Efemérides do dia 14 de Agosto

1947 - Paquistão assinala a independência, um dia antes da Índia.

1951 - É inaugurada em Lisboa a Igreja do Santo Condestável, no bairro de Campo de Ourique.

1956 - Morre o dramaturgo alemão Bertold Brecht. Tinha 58 anos.

1958 - O ditador português Oliveira Salazar reforça as pastas da Defesa e do Ultramar.

1960 - Morre, com 70 anos, o poeta, historiador e político português Jaime Cortesão.

1962 - As equipas de operários de Itália e França encontram-se no final das obras de perfuração do túnel do Monte Branco, que liga Chamonix, na Alta Saboia (França) a Courmayeur, no Vale de Aosta (Itália).

1971 -- Independência do Bahrain.

1973 - Terminam os bombardeamentos norte-americanos no Cambodja, pondo fim a 12 anos de combates na Indochina.

1974 -- Manifestação anticolonial em Lisboa. É pedida a independência dos territórios sob administração portuguesa.

1981 -- Morre, com 87 anos, o maestro austríaco Karl Boehm, referência na interpretação de obras dos períodos clássico e romântico.

1984 -- O Diário da República publica a Lei de bases da Segurança Social.

1991 - Morre a escritora Lídia da Fonseca, com 75 anos.

1992 - Morre o juiz norte-americano John Sirica, um dos protagonistas da investigação do caso Watergate. Tinha 88 anos.

1994 - Morre o escritor de origem búlgara Elias Canetti, autor de "Auto de Fé" e "O Poder e as Massas", Nobel da Literatura em 1981. Tinha 89 anos.

1995 - Morre o etnólogo português Fernando Galhano, aos 91 anos.-- Morre, com 84 anos, o maestro de origem romena Sergiu Celibidache.

1999 -- Começa a campanha para a consulta popular sobre a independência de Timor-Leste.

2001 -- Macedónios e albaneses assinam o acordo de paz de Skopje, aceite pela guerrilha albanesa.

2002 -Estreia do futebolista Cristiano Ronaldo no Sporting.

2003 - O Conselho de Segurança das Nações Unidas aprova a resolução 1500 que reconhece o Conselho de Governo transitório do Iraque e cria a Missão de Assistência das Nações Unidas (MANUI).

2004 - Rebeldes hutus atacam o campo de refugiados tutsi de Gatumba, no Burundi, provocando a morte a cerca de 160 pessoas.

2005 - Banda irlandesa U2 fecha digressão europeia em Lisboa e recebe a Ordem da Liberdade.

2006 - Entra em vigor o cessar-fogo que põe fim aos 34 dias da guerra israelo-libanesa. O balanço, no Líbano, aponta para mais de 1.200 mortos, perto de quatro milhares de feridos e cerca de um milhão de deslocados. Em Israel, a guerra provocou 116 mortos e 450 feridos.

2007 - A nova lei do tabaco que limita o fumo em locais públicos fechados e estabelece sanções até 250 mil euros para os infratores é publicada em Diário da República, para entrar em vigor em 2008.

2008 - Governo espanhol aprova plano de choque com 24 medidas económicas.

2009 - O Banco Privado Atlântico - Europa, de capitais maioritariamente angolanos, inicia a sua atividade em Portugal na área da banca de investimento.

2010 - O Museu da Arte Islâmica do Cairo, o maior do mundo, é inaugurado após oito anos de restauro.

2013 - O vice-presidente egípcio Mohamed El Baradei, com a tutela das relações exteriores, apresenta a sua demissão, após os confrontos violentos registados no Egito. Quase 280 pessoas morrem e duas mil ficaram feridas em resultado dos confrontos na cidade do Cairo e noutras províncias egípcias depois da ação policial contra os acampamentos dos apoiantes do Presidente deposto Mohamed Morsi.

2014 - O Tribunal Constitucional (TC) declara constitucional a norma que estabelece os cortes salariais no setor público nos anos de 2014 e 2015 e declara inconstitucionais reduções nos anos de 2016 a 2018.

2015 - O eurogrupo e o parlamento grego dão 'luz verde' ao terceiro resgate financeiro, no valor de até 86 mil milhões de euros até 2018. Tsipras fica debilitado ao perder o apoio de 47 deputados do Syriza.

2016 - O nadador norte-americano Michael Phelps conquista o seu 23.º título olímpico, terminando a carreira com a vitória dos Estados Unidos na final da estafeta de 4x100 metros estilos no Rio2016.

2017 - A China, principal parceiro e apoiante da economia norte-coreana, anuncia a suspensão das importações de ferro, chumbo e dos minérios destes dois metais e de produtos do mar da Coreia do Norte, aplicando as sanções decididas pela ONU.

results.title: Израелски медиуми: Шефот на ЦЕНТКОМ се залага за обновување на нападите врз Иран
results.body:
Шефот на американската Централна команда (ЦЕНТКОМ) се залага за обновување на нападите врз Иран, вклучително и напади врз нафтени, гасни и електроенергетски објекти, со цел зголемување на притисокот врз Техеран, објавија вчера израелските медиуми, пренесува Анадолу.

Израелскиот Канал 13, повикувајќи се на неименувани информирани политички извори, објави дека адмиралот Бред Купер го претставил предлогот за време на посетата на Израел минатата недела.

Купер присуствувал на состанокот на највисокиот оперативен форум на израелската војска, заедно со началникот на Генералштабот, Ејал Замир и други високи команданти, објави телевизијата.

За време на состанокот Купер повикал на обновување на борбите против Иран и напади врз националната инфраструктура, вклучително и објекти поврзани со гасната, нафтената и електроенергетската индустрија на земјата, според каналот.

"Нападите врз инфраструктурата во Иран ќе ги сменат правилата на играта, сериозно ќе ги погодат Иранците, а во сегашната ситуација тие нема да ги сменат своите ставови", бил цитиран Купер.

Според наводите, шефот на ЦЕНТКОМ им рекол на израелските воени претставници дека обновувањето на борбите би можело да стане единствена опција и дека САД можеби ќе треба да изведат заеднички напади со Израел врз Иран.

Според овие извори, Купер го претставил својот став и пред претседателот на Здружениот генералштаб на американската армија, генералот Ден Кејн, а предлогот бил пренесен и до претседателот Доналд Трамп.

Предлогот доаѓа и покрај извештаите од САД дека се намалила веројатноста за обновување на конфликтот со Иран, додека Вашингтон во последните денови ги засили напорите за прекин на борбите во регионот.

Во поврзан развој на настаните, ЦЕНТКОМ вчера соопшти дека ја формирал својата прва мултинационална единица за напади со беспилотни летала во соработка со неколку земји од Блискиот Исток.

Засега од САД нема коментар за тврдењата на израелската телевизија.

САД и Иран во април постигнаа прекин на огнот со посредство на Пакистан, а подоцна, на 17 јуни, потпишаа договор со кој започнаа преговори за постигнување конечен договор. Сепак, подоцна разговорите беа запрени поради несогласувањата околу безбедносните гаранции и непреченото пловење низ Ормускиот Теснец, една од најстратегиските траси во светот за глобалните енергетски резерви и трговија.

Од 8 до 24 јули САД и Иран разменија дополнителни воени напади, при што Вашингтон изврши напади врз цели во Иран. Техеран возврати со напади врз, како што ги опиша, американски воени објекти и опрема во неколку арапски земји, меѓу кои Јордан, Бахреин и Кувајт.

results.title: معامله پادشاه انگلیس با استرالیا/ چارلز سوم اسب قهرمانش را فروخت!
results.body:
تسنیم : شاه چارلز سوم، پادشاه انگلستان، اسب قهرمانش را در معاملهای بزرگ به استرالیا فروخت.

شاه چارلز سوم با فروش "پوینت آو لا" (Point Of Law)، اسب مسابقهای بسیار آیندهدار خود، موافقت کرد تا این اسب پس از جدایی از اصطبل جان گاسدن، راهی استرالیا شود؛ معاملهای که میتواند ارزشی چند میلیون پوندی داشته باشد.

پوینت آو لا که پیش از این در یک مسابقه گروه ۳ به نام "بحرین تروفی" در نیومارکت به پیروزی رسیده بود، قرار بود ماه آینده در سنت لجر، یکی از مسابقات کلاسیک مهم فصل، شرکت کند، اما پس از فروش، این برنامه منتفی شد.

این اسب نر در رویال اسکات سال گذشته در مسابقه گروه ۲ "کوئینز واز" چهارم شد، اما در آخرین حضورش با هدایت جیمز دویل، عملکردی درخشان داشت و در بحرین تروفی گروه ۳ به قهرمانی رسید.

پوینت آو لا اکنون زیر نظر چیرون ماهر، مربی مطرح استرالیایی، برای حضور در "کالفیلد کاپ" آماده خواهد شد. ماهر در رویال اسکات و نیومارکت عملکرد این اسب را از نزدیک دیده بود.

این اسب تاکنون بیش از ۱۳۰ هزار پوند جایزه مسابقات به دست آورده و با توجه به استعداد و سن پایینش، انتظار میرود قیمت فروش او به چند میلیون پوند برسد؛ هرچند رقم دقیق معامله اعلام نشده است.

پوینت آو لا پیش از سفر به استرالیا از اصطبل جان گاسدن خارج شده و برای آمادهسازی سفر، به اصطبل هری یوستیس در نیومارکت منتقل شده است.

قیمت اسبهای نخبه اروپایی در پی رقابت شدید خریداران بهشدت افزایش یافته و گروهی متشکل از دستکم پنج مالک برای به خدمت گرفتن پوینت آو لا حاضر به پرداخت مبلغ قابل توجهی شدهاند.

results.title: Hegseth: "SAD mogu neograničeno održavati blokadu iranskih luka"
results.body:
Američki ministar odbrane Pete Hegseth izjavio je u četvrtak da Sjedinjene Američke Države mogu neograničeno održavati blokadu iranskih luka, zahvaljujući mogućnosti rotiranja brodova u i iz regije prema potrebi.

"Blokadu možemo održavati onoliko dugo koliko je potrebno. Američka ratna mornarica može neograničeno održavati takvu blokadu jer ćemo, kao što smo to činili i do sada, nastaviti rotirati brodove", rekao je Hegseth novinarima u Panami, gdje je otputovao na završnu ceremoniju multinacionalne vojne vježbe.

"Nijedna druga država na svijetu, nijedna druga mornarica na svijetu nema sposobnost da postavi takav zid od čelika kakav ima američka mornarica, a potom i spremnost da ga koristi na način na koji smo mi to učinili", dodao je.

"Iran zna da kroz ovu blokadu ne može ni ući ni izaći, a zna i da ona nema vremensko ograničenje", rekao je Hegseth.

Američki predsjednik Donald Trump ranije ove sedmice izjavio je da SAD ima potpunu kontrolu nad Hormuškim moreuzom i obećao da će pomorska blokada biti nastavljena.

Iranski vojni zvaničnici, međutim, osporili su tvrdnje SAD-a o kontroli nad plovnim putem, a centralna vojna komanda Irana te navode je nazvala neosnovanim lažima i izmišljotinama.

"Lažne tvrdnje SAD-a o normalnom prolasku brodova kroz Hormuški moreuz, koje odražavaju nemoć i konfuziju vojske te zemlje, nisu ništa drugo do neistine i neosnovane laži", navela je vojna komanda u saopćenju koje je prenijela iranska državna televizija IRIB.

SAD i Iran dogovorili su u aprilu primirje uz posredovanje Pakistana, a potom su 17. juna potpisali sporazum kojim su pokrenuti pregovori o konačnom dogovoru. Međutim, pregovori su kasnije zastali zbog neslaganja u vezi sa sigurnosnim garancijama i slobodom plovidbe kroz Hormuški moreuz, jedan od najvažnijih svjetskih pravaca za snabdijevanje energentima i međunarodnu trgovinu.

Od 8. do 24. jula SAD i Iran razmijenili su nove vojne udare, pri čemu je Washington izveo napade na ciljeve unutar Irana. Teheran je odgovorio napadima na ono što je opisao kao američke vojne objekte i opremu u nekoliko arapskih zemalja, uključujući Jordan, Bahrein i Kuvajt.

results.title: روشتة برلمانية لتعظيم عوائد الموانئ وتحويل المحافظات الساحلية إلى قاطرة للنمو
results.body:
أكد النائب سليمان وهدان، رئيس الهيئة البرلمانية لحزب الجبهة الوطنية بمجلس النواب، أن تعظيم الاستفادة الاقتصادية من الموانئ المصرية والمحافظات الساحلية يجب أن يتحول إلى أولوية وطنية، باعتبارها أحد أهم مفاتيح زيادة موارد الدولة، ودعم الصادرات، وجذب الاستثمارات، وخلق فرص عمل جديدة، وتعزيز مكانة مصر كمركز إقليمي للتجارة والخدمات اللوجستية.

وقال " وهدان " فى تصريحات له : إن امتلاك مصر لموقع جغرافي فريد، وشبكة موانئ متطورة، وإطلالتها على البحرين المتوسط والأحمر، إلى جانب قناة السويس، يمنحها فرصة استثنائية للانتقال من مجرد دولة عبور للتجارة العالمية إلى مركز متكامل للتصنيع والتخزين والتوزيع والخدمات اللوجستية، مشددًا على ضرورة ألا تقتصر عوائد الموانئ على رسوم التداول والمناولة، وإنما تمتد إلى صناعات وخدمات وقيمة مضافة حولها.

إنشاء مناطق صناعية ولوجستية

وطرح رئيس

وتقدم النائب سليمان وهدان للحكومة بعدد من المقترحات الجديدة وغير التقليدية وفي مقدمتها إنشاء مناطق صناعية ولوجستية متخصصة ملاصقة للموانئ، بحيث يتم تصنيع وتجميع وتعبئة المنتجات قبل إعادة تصديرها، بما يضاعف القيمة الاقتصادية للحاوية الواحدة.

وإطلاق منصة رقمية موحدة للموانئ والمناطق اللوجستية تربط الجمارك والموانئ والنقل والمستودعات والمصدرين والمستوردين، بما يقلص زمن الإفراج ويخفض تكلفة التداول.

ودعا إلى إنشاء مراكز إقليمية لإعادة التصدير والتوزيع داخل المحافظات الساحلية، لتصبح مصر بوابة للمنتجات المتجهة إلى الأسواق الأفريقية والعربية والأوروبية وتخصيص حوافز استثمارية للمشروعات التي تقيم صناعاتها بالقرب من الموانئ وتستخدم النقل البحري والسككي، بما يخفف الضغط عن الطرق ويخفض التكلفة مع إنشاء صندوق لتنمية اقتصاد المحافظات الساحلية يمول من جزء من العوائد الإضافية الناتجة عن التوسع اللوجستي، ويوجه إلى تطوير البنية الأساسية، وتأهيل العمالة، ودعم المشروعات الصغيرة المرتبطة بالموانئ.

وشدد النائب سليمان وهدان على أن تطوير الموانئ يجب أن يسير بالتوازي مع تنمية المدن والمحافظات الساحلية، مؤكدًا أن الهدف النهائي هو خلق منظومة اقتصادية متكاملة تجعل من كل ميناء نقطة انطلاق للتصنيع والتصدير والاستثمار وفرص العمل، بما يعزز تنافسية الاقتصاد المصري ويحقق أقصى استفادة من الموقع الاستراتيجي للدولة

results.title: إيران تنشر صورا بالأقمار الاصطناعية لآثار ضرباتها للمواقع الأمريكية في الخليج
results.body:
نشرت إيران صورا التقطتها الأقمار الاصطناعية لآثار الضربات التي وجهتها للمواقع الأمريكية في دول الخليج.

وكشفت هذه الصور عن تدمير أهداف عسكرية واستخباراتية واقتصادية حساسة في الإمارات العربية المتحدة والبحرين، في وقت أظهرت فيه صور أخرى عودة طائرات التزود بالوقود الأمريكية إلى قاعدة "الظفرة" الإماراتية.

وبحسب الصور المنشورة، أسفرت الهجمات عن تدمير رادار من طراز AN/TPS-57 في قاعدة "الظفرة" الجوية بالإمارات العربية المتحدة، وهو الرادار المستخدم في مراقبة المجال الجوي ورصد التحركات الجوية. وفي البحرين، أظهرت الصور استهداف مركز بيانات مرتبط بالبنية التحتية الاستخباراتية الأمريكية.

ولم تقتصر الأضرار على الأهداف العسكرية، إذ وثقت الصور أيضا استهداف منشآت البنية التحتية للطاقة والصناعة في الإمارات العربية المتحدة، بما في ذلك محطة ضغط الغاز في مجمع "خَبْشَان" لتكرير النفط، فضلا عن منشأة إنتاج الكربون التابعة لشركة أمريكية.

وفي تطور مواز، أظهرت صور الأقمار الصناعية أن طائرات التزود بالوقود الأمريكية قد عادت هذا الأسبوع إلى قاعدة "الظفرة" الجوية في الإمارات، في خطوة تعكس استمرار النشاط العسكري الأمريكي في المنطقة رغم التصعيد المتبادل.

ويأتي نشر هذه الصور في سياق التصعيد العسكري المتزايد بين إيران والقوات الأمريكية في منطقة الخليج، حيث تسعى طهران من خلال توثيق آثار هجماتها إلى إبراز قدرتها على استهداف المنشآت الحيوية الأمريكية وحلفائها في المنطقة.
